Report_ID: Infants' heart rate during intervention (beats per minute)
Title: The Effect of Experience on Recognition of Mother's Voice in Preterm Infants
Author: Ahmadi Vastani, Zahedpasha, Jafarian Amiri, Khafri, Farhadi
Comment: Column headers in Table 2 are shifted in the extracted text; arm assignment confirmed from the Abstract ("the heart rate ... changed to 143.42 ± 2.85, 133.22 ± 2.15 and 138.28 ± 2.21" for mother's voice, stranger's voice and silent groups respectively). P = 0.016 is the omnibus one-way ANOVA across all three groups, not this pairwise contrast; Tukey post hoc found the significant pairwise difference only between mother's voice and stranger's voice (P = 0.012), so no pairwise p-value is recorded here. M_diff not computed because this is a three-arm one-way ANOVA rather than a simple two-group design. Table footnote states ± is SD, although the values (~2-3 bpm) are unusually small for heart rate and could plausibly be standard errors; recorded as SD per the paper's own footnote. N per group is the analysed n (20); 22 per group were randomized and 6 infants total excluded as outliers.
Participant type: Preterm infants (28 to <37 weeks gestation, birth weight 1000-2500 g) hospitalized in a NICU
Recruitment source: NICU of Bou-Ali-Sina medical training center, Sari, Northern Iran, May-November 2015
Outcome measurement: Mean heart rate (bpm) during the 10-minute intervention phase, Table 2 'During intervention' row
Outcome variable: Infants' heart rate during intervention (beats per minute)
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used in this row: stranger's voice group, n = 20 analysed (133.22 ± 2.15 bpm during intervention), extracted separately as E2; shared silent control (n = 20) is used in both comparisons
outcome_family: heart rate during the intervention session
effect_direction: unfavourable_to_music (HR higher with mother's live voice: 143.42 vs 138.28 bpm; MD = +5.14 bpm)

Heart rate is a daily mean of three measurements during the intervention period rather than a strictly within-session measurement. M_diff not computed because the reported F/p are omnibus across four arms.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Maternal voice (MV) group - recorded maternal voice at 45 dB in incubator, 3x/day for 30 min') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); N-INCONSISTENCY (multi-group): sum of additional_group_ns = 61 ≠ n_total(123) — verify all group Ns

Title: "The Original Sound": a new non-pharmacological approach to the postnatal stress management of preterm infants
Author: Tandoi et al.
Comment: Paper reports HR at baseline and days 1, 2 and 3; day 2 selected because it is the time point the paper reports as showing the significant group difference (day 1: TOS 131.1 (10.2) vs control 137.7 (11.7), p=0.09; day 3: 132.9 (9.4) vs 131.4 (10.8), p=0.65). "±"/parenthetical values are stated as SD in the table header. M_diff computed as group_2_mean - group_1_mean = 137.5 - 130.8 = 6.7 (control minus TOS); i.e. HR was 6.7 bpm LOWER in the TOS arm (MD = -6.7 bpm when expressed as treatment minus control). Measurements were taken after the TOS session rather than strictly during sound delivery.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('The Original Sound (TOS)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Preterm infants, gestational age 32 to <37 weeks, birth weight ≥1500 g, enrolled within 24 h of birth
Recruitment source: Department of Neonatology and NICU, "Filippo Del Ponte" Hospital, Varese, Italy
Outcome measurement: Heart rate in beats per minute recorded by monitor following nursing manoeuvres and TOS administration (day 2)
outcome_family: heart rate during the intervention session
effect_direction: favours_music (HR lower with recorded intrauterine sound: 130.8 vs 137.5 bpm; MD = -6.7 bpm, p=0.05)

Report_ID: Heart rate (bpm) — change from baseline period to music/silence period
Title: The Effects of Recorded Sedative Music on the Physiology and Behaviour of Premature Infants with a Respiratory Disorder
Author: Calabro, Wolfe, & Shoemark
Comment: Only the between-group difference in mean CHANGE from baseline to the music/silence period is reported (-0.9 bpm, 95% CI -5.0 to 3.2); no per-arm means or SDs for the music/silence period are given, so group_1_mean/group_2_mean and SDs are left empty. The values 156 (control) and 165 (music) in the table are BASELINE Day-1 means, not during-session values, and were therefore not entered as group means. SE_diff = (3.2 - (-5.0))/3.92 = 2.09, derived from the reported 95% CI. Per-group analysed Ns (9 control, 8 music) are derived from the Methods statement of 11 per group with 5 exclusions (2 control, 3 music); the paper does not state per-group analysed Ns directly. Sign convention per table note: positive values indicate a greater within-infant increase in the music group than control, so -0.9 means a non-significantly lower heart rate with music.
Medium: recorded sedative instrumental lullabies via mini-speakers
Content length: 20 minutes of music per day for 4 consecutive days within a 45-minute observation
Participant type: premature infants (34 weeks gestation) with chronic lung disorder and/or oxygen dependency
Recruitment source: Newborn services unit (NICU/special care nursery) of a large general hospital, Melbourne
Outcome measurement: Difference between music and control groups in mean within-infant change in heart rate from baseline to the music/silence period (robust standard errors across 4 daily observations)
Outcome variable: Heart rate (bpm) — change from baseline period to music/silence period
additional_group_ns: Randomised: 11 music, 11 control (N=22). Excluded from analysis: 2 control, 3 music → implied analysed 9 control, 8 music.
outcome_family: heart rate during the intervention session
effect_direction: favours_music (non-significant: MD = -0.9 bpm, 95% CI -5.0 to 3.2, p=0.64)

Title: Mothers' voices and white noise on premature infants' physiological reactions in a neonatal intensive care unit: A multi-arm randomized controlled trial
Author: Liao, Liu, Xie, Wang, Wu, Lin, Hu, He
Comment: No per-arm means, SDs or SEs for during-session heart rate are reported in the main text; those values appear only in Supplementary Table 2, which is not included in the provided text. Therefore group means/SDs and MD could not be extracted and were left empty. Only the omnibus 3-group repeated-measures ANOVA group effect (F=2.453, df1=2, p=0.091) is available; no df2 reported. Ns are randomised (ITT) Ns; 91 infants completed all measurements (routine care 30, white noise 30, mothers' voice 31 by subtraction, not stated per-arm as analysed). The white-noise arm shares the same routine-care control and is an auditory rather than music/voice intervention, so pre-identified effect E2 was not recorded separately.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ("Mothers' voice group (recorded maternal lullaby/voice, 20 min x3/day x4 days, 50-55 dB)") is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA excluded: comparison_type='mixed' is not between-group; N-INCONSISTENCY (multi-group): sum of additional_group_ns = 34 ≠ n_total(103) — verify all group Ns
Participant type: Medically stable premature infants (<37 weeks GA, birth weight ~1800 g) in incubators in a NICU
Recruitment source: NICU of a public women's and children's hospital, Fujian province, China
Outcome measurement: Mean heart rate during the 20-min intervention; repeated measures ANOVA group effect across the three arms
Outcome variable: Heart rate (bpm) during the 20-min intervention session
additional_group_ns: White noise group n=34 (auditory but non-music/non-voice arm; not extracted as a music/voice intervention and excluded to avoid double-counting the shared routine-care control)
outcome_family: heart rate during the intervention session
effect_direction: no_significant_difference (omnibus 3-group effect F=2.453, p=0.091; direction for maternal voice vs routine care not reported)

The reported P value and Cohen d (0.23, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.41) come from a repeated-measures mixed-model condition×time interaction in a within-subject crossover design (all 272 infants received every condition; no separate per-arm n). Title: Preterm infants with severe brain injury demonstrate unstable physiological responses during maternal singing with music therapy: a randomized controlled study
Author: Epstein S, Bauer S, Levkovits Stern O, Litmanovitz I, Elefant C, Yakobson D, Arnon S
Comment: Within-subject crossover design: the same 35 analysed infants contributed to both conditions, so the two "arms" are paired and not independent (flagged per plan's cross-over instruction; only combined paired data are reported, no first-period-only data). M_diff not computed because this is a paired within-subject comparison, not a simple two-group between-subjects design. Table 2 reports session-level mean heart rate (recorded every 5 min across baseline, intervention and recovery phases); the paper does not report heart rate separately for the 20-min intervention phase only (phase-level breakdown is given for HRV in Table 3 only). Per-arm Ns taken from the final analysed sample (35 of 40 enrolled); Table 2 itself does not state Ns. Direction is unfavourable to music: heart rate was HIGHER with SSC + maternal singing.; N-INCONSISTENCY: n_control(35) + n_treatment(35) = 70 ≠ n_total(35) — verify per-group Ns
Design Type: randomized within-subject crossover trial (participants as own controls)
Study Environment: NICU, quiet closed room with dimmed lights, ambient sound kept below 50 dB(A)
Medium: live maternal singing with guitar/vocal support by a certified music therapist during skin-to-skin contact
Content length: Sessions: 10 min baseline SSC + 20 min intervention phase + 10 min recovery; 3 sessions per condition per dyad
Topic of Content: Maternal-chosen songs/lullabies sung softly with slow tempo, attuned to infant cues
Participant type: Preterm infants born <32 weeks' gestation with severe brain injury (IVH grade 3 or 4 and/or PVL) and their mothers
Recruitment source: Tertiary level NIDCAP-certified NICU, Meir Medical Center, Kfar Saba, Israel (consecutive admissions 2014–2018)
Outcome measurement: Mean ± SD heart rate in beats per minute during study sessions (paired t-test)
outcome_family: heart rate during the intervention session
